sampling_model.design: Observational short panel with a fixed two-period design and exact cell-law inversion.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units drawn from the population law \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The binary predetermined covariate \(X_t\) is not randomized; its initial assignment and feedback may depend arbitrarily on \(u\).
sampling_model.overlap: The population sixteen-cell law is positive; the weak model allows zero latent assignment or feedback probabilities, while the strict model requires almost-everywhere positivity without a numerical lower bound.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cell law is estimated by multinomial frequencies; the finite-sample inversion uses simultaneous Clopper--Pearson intervals, and fixed-slope point estimation projects frequencies onto the attainable affine hull.

Theorem 3.1 characterizes the identified set by conditional moment equalities with generalized moments in a truncated Stieltjes cone.
Theorem 1 characterizes all feedback and heterogeneity robust moment conditions for the common parameter.
The main theorem replaces a latent distribution by a finite-dimensional identification-equivalent distribution for discrete covariates.

body.tldr: In a two-period binary logit panel with one predetermined binary covariate, continuous unrestricted heterogeneity, and arbitrarily heterogeneous feedback, the model-generated joint slope--APE fibers are characterized exactly by eight joint response-type measures and a finite quartic Stieltjes lift. The weak model uses fifty-six scalar variables with eight \(3\times3\) and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; strict almost-everywhere assignment and feedback positivity adds eight variables and eight \(6\times6\) common-range blocks. The same representation yields sharp fixed-slope endpoint programs with separate attainment tests, terminating algebraic membership and projection, and pointwise endpoint consistency on relative-interior attainable laws; direct Bonferroni inversion gives conservative exact multinomial whole-set coverage as a corollary. Uniform exact-set inference at rank-changing boundary laws and through \(c=1\) remains the explicit open problem.

project_justification.gap: The sharp unrestricted-feedback program of Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham is infinite-dimensional for continuous heterogeneity and is evaluated on support grids. The finite Stieltjes representation of Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell does not include a separately unknown heterogeneity-dependent feedback kernel or its reconstruction from one unconditional mixing law.
project_justification.niche: At two periods, joint feedback response types preserve legal sequential kernels, while the binary-logit likelihood shares a quartic denominator whose first five generalized moments are bounded for every heterogeneity law. This creates an exact low-order open-half-line moment problem with a finite simultaneous-support certificate.
project_justification.fill: The project first defines the weak and strict sharp fibers by laws generated from the published legal feedback classes, then proves their equivalence to forward-constructed joint response measures and reverse-reconstructed legal kernels, exact open-half-line and common-range PSD certificates, and sharp endpoint and attainment formulas; exact multinomial whole-set coverage is recorded only as the direct set-inversion corollary.

body.related_work: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1, define the sharp unrestricted-feedback identified set and motivate the response-density formulation; Theorem 4 supplies a strict finite-dimensional tightening of their continuous-support computation for \(T=2\). Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026), Theorems 3.1--3.2, supply the rational-mixture and truncated-Stieltjes method adapted here, but their known conditional likelihood does not contain the unknown feedback kernel. Curto and Fialkow (1991) and Bayer and Teichmann (2002) supply the moment-extension and finite-atomic tools used to treat singular open-half-line faces. Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2026) characterize feedback-robust moment equalities and explain why signed moment restrictions can exceed the positive sharp model. Gu, Russell, and Stringham (2026) give a complementary finite latent-cell method for discrete-outcome index models; their deterministic-cell enumeration does not remove the continuous logit mixing integral considered here. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) and Pakel and Weidner (2026) inform the unresolved rank-changing inference question. Arellano and Carrasco (2003) provide the predetermined-children labor-participation design that consumes exact feedback-robust bounds.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The strict common-support argument is existential and does not yet give an efficient atom-extraction routine. Real quantifier elimination establishes termination but not polynomial complexity or numerical stability. Positive observed cells do not imply strict latent assignment or feedback, a closed lifted cone need not have a closed linear image, and endpoint solver values therefore require the stated inclusion tests.
body.honest_scope: The model-generated weak and strict fibers are the primitive identified objects. Their exact finite-certificate equivalences, legal-kernel converses, fixed-slope endpoints, algebraic decision, and relative-interior pointwise consistency are theorem-level targets. Finite-sample whole-set coverage is a direct Bonferroni set-inversion corollary and carries no independent inference kernel. Boundary-uniform inference, joint consistency through \(c=1\), efficient certified numerical extraction, arbitrary \(T\), Markov feedback restrictions, and multinomial outcomes remain open. No numerical overlap margin, tail moment, latent density, or support grid is imposed.
